locators.locator: Gaming generally is an unrelated trade or business unless a specific exception applies; use the linked Publication 3079 and IRC/Regulation references for the detailed route.

IRC 513(f) and Treas. Reg. 1.513-5 route qualifying bingo only when wagers, winner determination and prize distribution occur in the presence of all players; legality and local for-profit activity conditions also apply.

Gaming conducted off-site or with the general public, state/local illegality, third-party sponsorship, incomplete game reporting, and reporting gaming revenues net instead of gross are listed as review indicators.
For 501(c)(7) social clubs, distinguish member or bona fide guest income from nonmember/general-public income and apply the separate UBTI rule.

limitations: Federal tax guidance is not US GAAP revenue or liability guidance.
State and local gaming legality, license terms, entity exemption section and actual game facts remain unverified.
The live page does not establish a tax filing result for a particular organization.

research_questions.question: How should an event producer connect advance tickets, refunds, event completion and cash settlement?
research_questions.scope: Selected US live-event producer controlling admission service; illustrative 2026 calendar-year close. Ticket agent and venue custody are counterroles.
research_questions.answer: Record advance ticket consideration separately from earned admission revenue and refund liability. question_rows.answer: Identify the promised sponsor deliverable, rights grant, control and counterparty before classifying the amount. An acknowledgment or service can be exchange consideration; a donor restriction requires contribution facts; an agent remittance can be customer money rather than the agent's revenue.

question_rows.question: How should museum admissions or memberships be separated from donor-restricted mission support?
question_rows.scope: Selected US museum or mission-based nongovernmental NFP with membership access, admissions and restricted exhibit support; illustrative 2026 close.
question_rows.answer: Treat membership or admission as an access exchange population under the stated service period and retain donor-restricted support in the restricted contribution and release workflow. The synthetic case recognizes one delivered membership month and a release tied to eligible exhibit spending.

question_rows.question: What rights and period evidence must support an event or museum licensed-content amount?
question_rows.scope: Selected US event, performing-rights, museum reproduction or membership-access arrangement; rights period is contractual first.
question_rows.answer: Retain the signed rights or access grant, territory, media, term, renewal/termination, usage and counterparty approval. Reconcile any license consideration or royalty to the contractual period and usage report; statutory or public source duration does not replace the agreement.

question_rows.question: Which gaming records and federal tax exceptions must a selected exempt organization retain?
question_rows.scope: Selected US exempt organization or recreation operator conducting gaming; federal tax routing only, with state/local legality and entity exemption facts unresolved.
question_rows.answer: Keep gross gaming receipts, prize payouts, related disbursements, session and participant evidence, license/legality evidence and the federal filing route separate. Test trade/business, regularity, relation to exempt purpose and any applicable bingo, volunteer, public-entertainment or member exception; do not use a game label as the conclusion.

question_rows.question: How should a recreation venue or gaming agent keep customer wagers and settlement distinct from earned revenue?
question_rows.scope: Selected US venue, platform or agent holding customer wagers or ticket proceeds for a principal; illustrative custody counterrole only.
question_rows.answer: Reconcile customer funds received, remitted, outstanding and settlement fees in separate populations. The counterrole ledger records receipt and remittance as a wager liability and does not infer earned gaming or ticket revenue without control and contract evidence.
